original.target_description: Original Study 1a; full original paper not acquired through allowed routes.

replication.target_description: Replication 2, leisure-frame book-browsing task: goal conflict versus no conflict; natural log of seconds, capped at 300 seconds.

n.sample_role: Participants in the leisure-frame simple-effect comparison. Whole-study post-exclusion N is 1,127; frame-specific analytic n is not printed in the report or figure.
n.exclusions: Failed attention check; survey longer than 30 minutes; duplicate MTurk IDs or IP addresses; actual versus reported MTurk ID mismatch. Times over 300 seconds winsorized to 300 seconds.
n.quote: After exclusions, we wound up with 1,008 participants in Replication 1 and 1,127 participants in Replication 2

es.location: Results, second (leisure) hypothesis paragraph; ds ordered Replication 1 then Replication 2
es.quote: the effect sizes we observed (ds = -.13 and -.15) are much smaller than what was reported in the original (d = -.34)

p.location: Results figure, Original vs. Replication Results: Time Spent Book Browsing (Log), Replication 2, Leisure-Frame

reported_success.location: Results, final paragraph before What About Data Quality?
reported_success.quote: On balance, then, these replications were not successful.

notes: Original full paper unavailable; original statistics in Data Colada are secondary summaries and were not substituted for primary original extraction. Replication source title and target match verified. The report gives only whole-study post-exclusion N, not the analytic sample size of the assigned frame-specific test. Replication effect sizes and p values refer to the same frame-specific contrast on log time. Reported success is the replication authors' overall verdict on both replications; original authors' feedback expresses a different interpretation. Replication 1 pre-registration was prepared but not officially submitted (footnote 2).
